user.title: Connect to Smart Meter Gateway
user.description: Enter your SMGW HAN interface credentials. The integration will fetch certified daily meter readings once per day.

data_description.url: URL of the SMGW HAN interface (default: https://192.168.100.100/cgi-bin/hanservice.cgi)
data_description.tariff_zones:
One entry per switch point in the format "HH:MM zone name", starting at 00:00; the last entry runs until midnight. Example Octopus Go: "00:00 Go" and "05:00 Standard".
Equal zone names share one sensor: "00:00 Standard", "02:00 Low", "06:00 Standard", "12:00 Low" creates two sensors — "Standard" sums 00:00-02:00 and 06:00-12:00, "Low" sums 02:00-06:00 and 12:00-24:00.
Minutes must be 00, 15, 30 or 45.
data_description.update_time: Time of day for the automatic daily data fetch
data_description.device_name: Leave empty unless you set this integration up multiple times against the same SMGW (e.g. separate logins for grid import and feed-in). In that case enter a distinct name to tell the devices apart.

select_meter.title: Select meter
select_meter.description: Your SMGW exposes multiple meters. Pick which physical meter this entry shall represent in Home Assistant. If you want to monitor both, just add another entry after this setup and pick the other meter there.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate SMGW
reauth_confirm.description: The SMGW credentials are no longer valid. Please enter updated credentials.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot connect to the SMGW. Check the URL and network connection.
error.duplicate_login: Another configured entry already uses this meter and username combination.
error.parse_error: Could not parse the SMGW response. Please double-check the username and password. If the credentials are correct, wait up to 15 minutes and try again.
error.invalid_zone_entry: Each entry must have the format "HH:MM zone name", e.g. "05:00 Standard".
error.zone_too_few: Define at least two entries (00:00 plus one switch point).

error.zone_minute_grid: Minutes must be 00, 15, 30 or 45 (the SMGW records on a 15-minute grid).

menu_options.export: Export SMGW data for a custom time range

settings.title: SMGW Settings
settings.description: Update credentials, tariff time and fetch time.

data_description.url: URL of the SMGW HAN interface (default: https://192.168.100.100/cgi-bin/hanservice.cgi)
data_description.tariff_zones:
One entry per switch point in the format "HH:MM zone name", starting at 00:00; the last entry runs until midnight. Example Octopus Go: "00:00 Go" and "05:00 Standard".
Equal zone names share one sensor: "00:00 Standard", "02:00 Low", "06:00 Standard", "12:00 Low" creates two sensors — "Standard" sums 00:00-02:00 and 06:00-12:00, "Low" sums 02:00-06:00 and 12:00-24:00.
Minutes must be 00, 15, 30 or 45.
Note on statistics history: each zone gets its own consumption sensor. Home Assistant identifies these sensors by their position in the list (first zone, second zone …), not by the name you enter.
Changing times or appending further zones at the end is therefore safe – existing sensors keep their history. But if you reorder or rename the zones so that a different zone now occupies a previously used position, the new zone's data is appended to the old zone's data in the Home Assistant history, i.e. the sensor's statistics get mixed.
data_description.update_time: Time of day for the automatic daily data fetch
data_description.device_name: Custom name (e.g. "SMGW Import" / "SMGW Export") for the case where you run multiple logins against the same SMGW as separate entries. Otherwise leave empty.

export.title: Export consumption and feed-in data
export.description: Choose a period and which files to create. The next step lets you fine-tune the exact date range.

data_description.period: The next step pre-fills the date range from this choice; you can still edit it there.

export_dates.title: Confirm time range
export_dates.description: Adjust the range if needed, then submit to start the export. Tip: to include the last day's closing reading, set 'To' to 00:15 of the following day.

export_readings.name: Export readings (custom range)
export_readings.description: Fetch the SMGW meter readings for a custom From/To range. Returns the data as a response variable and can additionally create the signed CMS original file, a CSV and/or an Excel file, downloadable via the links (shown at the top of the response variable).

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The SMGW meter device to query. In scripts and dashboards you can leave this empty if you have only one SMGW.

from_datetime.name: From
from_datetime.description: Start of the time range (date and time).

to_datetime.name: To
to_datetime.description: End of the time range. Tip: to include the closing reading of the last day, set this to 00:15 of the following day.

download_cms.name: Download certified CMS file
download_cms.description: Also save the signed CMS file exactly as delivered by the SMGW (the tamper-evident original).

write_csv.name: Create CSV
write_csv.description: Also create the raw readings as a semicolon-separated CSV file.

write_xlsx.name: Create Excel (XLSX)
write_xlsx.description: Also create an Excel workbook with raw data, daily end values and tariff zones.

export_period.name: Export readings (period preset)
export_period.description: Fetch the SMGW meter readings for a ready-made period. The range, including the closing reading of the last day, is computed automatically. Identical outputs and download options as the custom-range export.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The SMGW meter device to query. In scripts and dashboards you can leave this empty if you have only one SMGW.

period.name: Period
period.description: The time range to export. The end is set automatically to capture the closing reading of the last day.

download_cms.name: Download certified CMS file
download_cms.description: Also save the signed CMS file exactly as delivered by the SMGW (the tamper-evident original).

write_csv.name: Create CSV
write_csv.description: Also create the raw readings as a semicolon-separated CSV file.

write_xlsx.name: Create Excel (XLSX)
write_xlsx.description: Also create an Excel workbook with raw data, daily end values and tariff zones.

no_recent_data.title: SMGW is not delivering current data
no_recent_data.description: The Smart Meter Gateway returned no (complete) daily values for {date} (last successful: {last_date}). Login and connection work fine — the gateway simply isn't providing new daily data (e.g. after a meter or account change). Existing sensor values are kept. This notice disappears automatically as soon as a day is fetched successfully again.
